source.title: Preliminary Results on Building Graphs from SAEs

record.file_problem: The post is present, but some embedded math values and figure details are missing from the supplied text (for example, the repeat threshold and some component sizes).
record.tranche_reason: The post measures conditional-dependence structure among SAE features, but does not test any of the listed claims about superposition, polysemanticity, LLM feature recovery, canonical SAE units, or feature dimensionality.
record.gate_note: The reported edge counts and estimated FDRs concern stability of a conditional-dependence graph under resampling. They are recorded as related geometry findings, not as evidence for a listed claim version. The post also describes qualitative clusters, but missing figure/math details prevent recording their omitted sizes as results.
record.test_reason: The post builds nodewise-LASSO conditional-dependence graphs over Gemma Scope SAE features and reports edge stability under resampling against shuffle nulls. It does not measure superposition, polysemanticity, whether SAEs recover features, whether SAE features are canonical units, or feature dimensionality. Its observation that tiny components are mostly duplicated features is qualitative, uncounted and only incidental, so it is not a test of V5.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct. The author presents this as a proof of concept: resampling-stable conditional-dependence edges and coherent-looking small modules that align only weakly with cosine similarity. The method approximates a precision graph and needs refinement.
record.recipe_differences: The post develops a nodewise-LASSO conditional-dependence graph procedure for SAE activations; it does not reproduce the original superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The reported graph depends on pre-screening by activation correlations and has hyperparameters the author says need further sweeps or methodological changes. The author also notes that cross-dataset effects remain to be studied.

fits_no_version.finding: Among the 302 stable edges (227 nodes), most tiny connected components were duplicated SAE features with strong cosine similarity, so the author filtered them out. No count is given.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Gemma Scope SAE features (gemma2:27b, layer 10, width 131k) include redundant, near-duplicate features that show up as tightly linked tiny components in a conditional-dependence graph.

fits_no_version.finding: The edge counts in rows r1–r7 show sharply more edges than the shuffle null at 2 or more repeats (estimated FDR 3.47e-02 at 2 repeats). The resulting standalone components look linguistically coherent, and edge strength correlates only weakly with cosine similarity.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: SAE feature activations have a sparse, resampling-stable conditional-dependence structure that only weakly follows decoder cosine similarity.

record.problems: The author calls the work preliminary and notes it is not a true precision graph because SAE activations are not Gaussian; the method depends on correlation pre-screening and hyperparameters; stability is only under resampling on the same dataset and does not establish feature faithfulness; only a single null resampling per trial was used; the results shown are for one SAE layer and one dataset. Some figure and math details are missing from the supplied text.
record.rows_left_out: No additional quantitative rows omitted. Qualitative cluster details are not recorded where the supplied text omits their node counts or relies on unavailable figures.

untested.parts: All: no toy models, sparsity transition or geometry.
All: no analysis of where polysemanticity comes from.
All: SAE features are taken as given. Their recoverability, or spread across neurons, is not tested.

Completeness, stability across SAE training runs or sizes, and canonicality are not measured. Stability here means edge stability under data resampling. The author says this does not show feature faithfulness.
All: features are not tested for multi-dimensionality.

missing.what: Component sizes from manual inspection of the 302-edge stable subset: 227 nodes, one large component of 98 nodes, and standalone components of 9, 9, 7, 5 and 5 nodes. The rows_left_out field wrongly says these sizes are unavailable.
missing.locator: Initial Results, Small components / Large component

record.verdict_notes: The rows' values match the table. The post's links to feature splitting, absorption and SAE feature geometry are motivation only. No row bears on any version.

versions.untested_parts: Toy-model superposition, sparsity-dependent transitions, and regular geometry.
Whether capacity competition causes polysemanticity or gives important features dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemanticity arises without capacity pressure.
Whether LLM features spread across neurons or can be recovered by a dictionary.
Whether SAE features are complete, stable, or canonical units; graph resampling stability is not a test of feature faithfulness.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.
